items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances in additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances in additional AWS Regions. Both M8i and R8i instances are now available in Asia Pacific (New Zealand) and Canada West (Calgary), and R8i instances are now available in Europe (Milan, Stockholm, and Zurich) and Israel (Tel Aviv).

These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The M8i and R8i instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances.

M8i and R8i instances are available for Amazon RDS for Oracle in Bring Your Own License model for Oracle Database Enterprise Edition (EE) and Oracle Database Standard Edition 2 (SE2). For EE, instances are available in sizes from large to 48xlarge, as well as bare metal sizes metal-48xl and metal-96xl. For SE2, instances are available in sizes from large to 4xlarge and bare metal sizes metal-48xl and metal-96xl. Refer to Amazon RDS for Oracle Pricing for available instance configurations, pricing, and region availability.

items.title: Haiku 5.5 now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
A new Anthropic model is now available in the Kiro IDE and CLI for the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. With Haiku 5.5, all three Claude 5.5 models are now available in Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US).

Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest model in the Claude 5.5 family. It's a clear step up from Claude Haiku 4.5, built for work that runs in large volumes and needs quick responses. Developers can use it to summarize and compact long context, classify and route requests, process text in bulk, and make small, targeted edits across many files. It also works well as a review subagent that runs in parallel, while Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 take on harder planning and coding work. Haiku 5.5 uses adaptive thinking across five effort levels from low to max, with medium as the default. It's available with a 1M context window and a 0.06x credit multiplier. Requests over 100K tokens are billed at a 0.3x multiplier.

Ensure your IDE or CLI is updated to the latest version, then restart it to access the new model from the model selector. For more details, visit the GovCloud documentation, the monitoring and tracking guide, or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the Kiro product page.

items.title: Amazon RDS now supports per snapshot billing
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon RDS supports per snapshot billing for Amazon RDS snapshots. Per snapshot billing allows you to get the cost of each individual snapshot.

Previously, RDS snapshot charges were aggregated at the database instance level on the Cost and Usage report as well as the Cost Explorer. This meant that while understanding the snapshot charges, you could only see the aggregate view at the database instance instead of drilling down to each individual snapshot. Now, you can use cost allocation tags on your snapshots to see exactly how much each snapshot costs, giving you a better understanding of your backups spend and budgets. Per snapshot billing is enabled by default on all RDS snapshots for no additional charge.

Per snapshot billing is available for all Amazon RDS engines in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, please visit our documentation.

items.title: Amazon Quick on desktop now uses your organization's existing Amazon Quick sign-in
items.summary:
For organizations that use Amazon Quick, the desktop application now signs users in with the same sign-in method the organization already uses for Quick on the web. Administrators no longer need to register an OIDC application in their identity provider or set up separate desktop sign-in before users can get started. If a user can sign in to Quick on the web, that user can sign in to the desktop application.

To turn on desktop access, an administrator adds the desktop connector once in the Amazon Quick console. Users then enter their Quick account name, choose Sign In, and finish signing in through their browser. This works for accounts that use IAM Identity Center, IAM federation, or native Amazon Quick users. If your organization wants to manage desktop sign-in separately, you can still set up a dedicated identity provider configuration with providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, or Ping Identity.

Amazon Quick on desktop is available in AWS Regions that support the full Amazon Quick feature set.

To get started, see Amazon Quick on desktop in the Amazon Quick User Guide.

items.title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.10 is now generally available
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.10. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by the MySQL community. For more details, refer to the Aurora MySQL 8.4 and MySQL 8.4.10 release notes.

Aurora MySQL 8.4.10 adds support for global transaction identifiers (GTID) tags, which lets you assign a user-defined tag to GTIDs to help you identify and group related transactions in binary log replication. This release also adds support for a maximum of 50,000 simultaneous connections per DB instance, which allows connection-intensive applications to scale without adding a connection pooling layer. Learn more about maximum connections best practices in the Amazon Aurora MySQL User Guide.  

You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon Aurora User Guide. This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Aurora MySQL is available.

Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full MySQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at Aurora's getting started page.

items.title: AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event sources
items.summary:
AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event source mappings (ESM), for Kafka clusters that customers run themselves and for managed offerings such as Confluent Cloud. Customers can now scale processing for Kafka workloads beyond the partition count of a topic, increasing throughput during traffic spikes and improving processing resilience.

Customers building event-driven Kafka workloads for use cases such as image and video encoding, fraud detection, notification delivery, and telemetry ingestion treat each event as an independent unit of work, where processing speed matters more than strict ordering. Previously, Kafka ESMs used the Kafka consumer group protocol, which assigns each partition to exactly one consumer within a consumer group. Customers needing higher parallelism had to over-partition topics or move traffic to a separate queuing system, adding infrastructure to operate and producer code to maintain. Queue support for self-managed Kafka ESMs is built on Kafka share groups, which are generally available in Apache Kafka 4.2. This launch enables multiple event pollers to consume concurrently from the same partition, with each event poller supporting up to 10 concurrent invocations. This decouples parallelism from partition count with no changes to producers, topic configuration, or function code. As a result, customers get higher throughput during traffic spikes and more resilient processing, because a slow or failed event no longer holds up other events in the same partition. Queue mode does not preserve partition ordering and is intended for workloads that do not require it.

This capability requires a Kafka cluster with share groups enabled, such as Apache Kafka 4.2 or later, and is available in all AWS commercial Regions where self-managed Kafka ESM is available. To get started, create a self-managed Kafka ESM with ConsumptionMode set to Queue through the AWS Management Console, Lambda API, AWS CLI, AWS CloudFormation, AWS SAM, or AWS CDK. Standard Lambda pricing applies. Customers who configure provisioned mode for their self-managed Kafka ESM also pay for Event Poller Unit (EPU) usage. To learn more, see the AWS Lambda Developer Guide and AWS Lambda pricing.

items.title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 3.14 (compatible with MySQL 8.0.46) is generally available
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 3 (compatible with MySQL 8.0) supports MySQL 8.0.46, which includes community MySQL fixes and Aurora-specific improvements. In addition to operational improvements, Aurora MySQL 3.14 introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in-transit. For detailed information on this release, refer to Aurora MySQL 3 and MySQL 8.0.46 release notes.

You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Aurora MySQL is available.

Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full MySQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at Aurora’s getting started page.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in flows
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to invoke Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in customer experience flows through the new 'External Tool' block. With this launch, you can connect flows to third-party applications through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and reuse the same tools used by your agentic experiences to retrieve data or trigger actions, without writing custom Lambda functions. For example, when a customer contacts a financial institution about a recent transaction, a flow can use the External Tool block to retrieve relevant context from a third-party application, such as case history from their CRM system, or transaction details from a banking platform.

This feature is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). To learn more about this feature, refer to the administrator guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block, giving you more control over how your customer experience flows react to real-time data changes. In addition to waiting for a Lambda function to complete, you can now wait until a Connect Case field meets a specified condition or an External Tool invocation completes. This enables you to wait for critical information before advancing an interaction, reducing unnecessary transfers and saving time for both your end-customers and agents. For example, you can hold a flow until a refund status field is updated on a case, then automatically resume and route the interaction based on the outcome. 

To learn more about this feature, refer to the administrator guide and availability of Connect Customer features by Region. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: EC2 Amazon Machine Images can now be scanned for vulnerabilities through Amazon Inspector
items.summary:
Amazon Inspector now extends its vulnerability scanning to EC2 Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), enabling you to identify software vulnerabilities in your AMIs without launching instances or installing additional software. This helps you fix issues at the source before AMIs are used to launch instances across your fleet.

With this capability, you can run continuous evaluations to monitor your AMI catalog for newly discovered vulnerabilities, or perform targeted one-time scans for specific AMIs directly from the EC2 Console. You can enable AMI scanning for an account or across your entire organization in Amazon Inspector. For AWS Security Hub customers, you can enable AMI scanning as an add-on across your organization, and findings are also delivered to Security Hub. Based on the scan results, you can enable the Allowed AMIs setting and specify security criteria that AMIs must meet to be available within your account and enforce this setting across the entire organization using Declarative Policies. Customers building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder can integrate scanning directly into their pipelines and restrict distribution of AMIs that do not meet their security standards.

AMI Scanning helps you detect and remediate vulnerabilities earlier in your deployment pipeline, reducing the risk of deploying compromised compute resources. Security teams can now establish a consistent vulnerability scanning process across all AMIs improving their security posture before instances are launched.

This capability is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon Inspector is available. To learn more, see the EC2 User Guide, Amazon Inspector User Guide, the Amazon Inspector pricing page, and the Amazon Inspector product page.

items.title: Amazon Textract now available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich)
items.summary:
Amazon Textract is now available in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich) Regions. Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents, going beyond simple optical character recognition (OCR) to identify and extract text and structured data.

At launch in these Regions, Amazon Textract supports text detection and document analysis. This includes the DetectDocumentText, AnalyzeDocument, StartDocumentTextDetection, GetDocumentTextDetection, StartDocumentAnalysis, and GetDocumentAnalysis operations. The AnalyzeExpense, AnalyzeID, and AnalyzeLending operations, and Custom Queries (adapters), are not available in these Regions at this time.

With this launch, Amazon Textract is available in a total of 18 AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), the AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions, and the newly added Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich) Regions.

To learn more, see the Amazon Textract product page and the Amazon Textract Developer Guide. For pricing and Region availability, see the Amazon Textract pricing page and Amazon Textract endpoints and quotas.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront now supports self-service increases in AWS Service Quotas
items.summary:
Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Service Quotas, so you can view, monitor, and request increases for 28 CloudFront quotas from the Service Quotas console or API.

Until now, increasing a quota on resources such as distributions, cache policies, origins, or alternate domain names meant opening a support case and waiting for manual review. If you have AWS Business Support or higher, requests for limit increases within published thresholds are now approved automatically. For example, you can raise your distribution quota from 500 to 1,000, or the number of alternate domain names per distribution from 100 to 500, without opening a support case. Some quotas also publish usage metrics to Amazon CloudWatch every 5 minutes, so you can set alarms and request an increase before you reach a limit..

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudFront is supported.

To get started, visit the Service Quotas console to view and request increases for your CloudFront quotas. To learn more, see Amazon CloudFront quotas in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.

items.title: Announcing an updated text detection model for Amazon Textract
items.summary:
Amazon Textract now provides an updated text detection model that improves accuracy, expands language support, and enhances multilingual table extraction. The updated model applies to the DetectDocumentText and AnalyzeDocument APIs and requires no changes to your Amazon Textract API requests or response schema. Your applications are served by the updated model automatically, so you can continue calling Amazon Textract exactly as before.

The updated model expands language coverage to more than 40 languages, including Albanian, Arabic, Basque, Belarusian, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Luxembourgish, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian Cyrillic, Serbian Latin, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Turkmen, and Ukrainian, enabling reliable processing of previously unsupported scripts. Accuracy improvements include enhanced long-word recognition and handwriting detection. Additionally, multilingual table extraction is more robust on merged cells, skewed or rotated tables, and partial or corrupted tables. These improvements help you accurately process invoices, forms, identity documents, and other multilingual or complex documents, including those with tables, at scale.

The updated Amazon Textract model is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Textract is available. To learn more, see the Amazon Textract product page and the Amazon Textract Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock expands API support and introduces Cross-Region Inferencing for OpenAI models in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock now supports the OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (Terra and Luna) on the bedrock-runtime endpoint, with support for the Responses, Converse, and Chat Completions APIs in AWS GovCloud (US). It also adds support for Cross-Region Inference, allowing customers to use Cross-Region Inference within AWS GovCloud (US) regions to access higher throughput and increased redundancy.  

Cross-Region Inference automatically routes inference requests across both AWS GovCloud (US) Regions to give you higher throughput, without you needing to manage capacity across multiple Regions. Cross-Region Inference within AWS GovCloud (US) routes requests across both regions so you can scale while maintaining US data sovereignty, giving you the broadest access to Bedrock capacity and the highest throughput during demand spikes. This launch also expands API support; you can use OpenAI GPT models with the Responses API, Chat Completions API, and the Converse API on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. Because these native OpenAI APIs now run on bedrock-runtime, the models work with the same account-level controls you already use for other models on Bedrock: usage appears in Bedrock model invocation logging (deliverable to Amazon S3 or Amazon CloudWatch Logs) and in Amazon CloudWatch metrics covering invocation counts, token counts, latency, throttles, and errors, and it is itemized in AWS Cost Explorer and the AWS Cost and Usage Report so you can attribute spend by model.

Cross-Region Inference for OpenAI models is available in all AWS Regions where OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock are offered. To get started, review the model cards for GPT-5.6 (Terra and Luna) in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

items.title: Web Search now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Kiro web search gives the agent real-time access to current information on the internet, so its answers draw on up-to-date search results and page content. The agent uses web search automatically when a question involves recent changes or topics beyond the model's training data. Answers that use web results include citations.

Kiro enterprise administrators can turn off web search and web fetch for their organization from the Kiro console under Settings. Teams can also remove web tools from individual custom agents, or block them with capability-based permission rules.

For more details, visit the AWS GovCloud (US) documentation, the monitoring and tracking guide, or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the Kiro product page.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts, helping agents resume work without losing progress when connectivity is interrupted or when their browser is accidentally closed or refreshed. When agents return, their drafts are restored with the message body, recipients, subject line, and attachment references intact. Customers can also access saved draft data in their Amazon S3 buckets to build integrations with other applications.

items.title: Daybreak Red from OpenAI now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
items.summary:
Security teams need powerful tools to find vulnerabilities, test exploits, and build defenses. Daybreak Red from OpenAI is now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East), bringing advanced AI to this work.

 

Part of OpenAI’s Daybreak cyber defense initiative, Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber is built for authorized vulnerability research, exploit reproduction, and mitigation development. It gives verified defenders more room to investigate complex security problems, with fewer refusals for this work and stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls.

Daybreak Red runs on Bedrock’s next-generation inference engine, with zero-operator access enforced at the chip. Your inference data is not used to train models, and you do not need to share your Daybreak Red data with OpenAI.

 

The model is available in US East (Ohio) and AWS GovCloud (US-East). Access to the model requires enrollment in Daybreak access from OpenAI. To get started, contact OpenAI or your AWS account team about Daybreak eligibility. Once approved, work with your AWS account team to enable access. Learn more in the blog.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront now provides viewer ISP and post-quantum TLS details
items.summary:
Amazon CloudFront can now forward two new optional headers to your origin. The CloudFront-Viewer-ISP header contains the name of the viewer's internet service provider (ISP), so you can see which network a request came from. The CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details header describes the cryptography used on each viewer's TLS connection, so you can see whether a connection used post-quantum cryptography (PQC).

With CloudFront-Viewer-ISP, you can break down traffic and performance by network. You can also isolate unusual traffic from a single provider. CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details includes the key exchange, signature scheme, and signature public key type for each connection. You can use it to measure the share of viewers that actually connect with PQC and identify clients that do not yet do so. To forward either header to your origin, add it to an origin request policy and attach the policy to your distribution.

To get started, see adding CloudFront headers and controlling origin requests with a policy in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide

items.title: Amazon MSK now supports TLS 1.3 for data in transit
items.summary:
Amazon MSK now supports version 1.3 of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol for MSK Provisioned clusters through encryption policies. TLS 1.3 delivers faster, more secure encryption for streaming data and is increasingly required by compliance frameworks and enterprise security standards. It is also one of the prerequisites for post-quantum cryptography for protecting data against attacks that collect encrypted traffic now with the intent to decrypt it later.

Customers can opt in to TLS 1.3 by selecting a named security policy in their MSK cluster configuration, with no change to existing clusters until a policy is applied. A named security policy defines which TLS version and cipher suites a cluster can accept. With this launch, Amazon MSK provides a set of policies customers can select and any connection that does not meet the selected policy requirements is rejected. This allows customers to stay in control of their security and compliance posture. Policies that support both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 allow connections to negotiate the highest version the client supports allowing clients that support TLS 1.3 to connect on it immediately while clients on TLS 1.2 continue to connect on TLS 1.2. This lets customers upgrade their clients at their pace before applying a stricter policy. Customers can also select stricter policies that align closer with their compliance requirements to restrict connections to TLS 1.3 only.

This capability is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Provisioned is available. To learn more, see the Amazon MSK documentation.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle no longer requires automatic minor version upgrades for JVM, Spatial, Locator, and OLAP options
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now lets you turn off automatic minor version upgrades on new and existing DB instances that use the JVM, Spatial, Locator, or OLAP option. Previously, these options required automatic minor version upgrades to be enabled.

With this change, you decide when to apply minor version upgrades to DB instances using these options. If you turn off automatic minor version upgrades, we recommend that you apply new minor versions regularly so your DB instances keep the latest Oracle security fixes. To keep automatic minor version upgrades turned on and still control the order in which your environments are upgraded, you can use AWS Organizations upgrade rollout policy.

This change is available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more about options available in Amazon RDS for Oracle, see Adding options to Oracle DB instances in the Amazon RDS User Guide.

items.title: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions
items.summary:
AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. When you enable it, CloudFront adds the script tag for the AWS WAF JavaScript SDK to the HTML it serves, with no change to your application code, build process, or deployment. The SDK supplies the client-side signals used by three AWS WAF managed rule groups: Bot Control at the targeted inspection level, Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), and Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP).

Previously, supplying those signals required you to add a script tag to every page of every application you wanted to protect, and to maintain that tag across releases. For teams running many applications, or serving pages produced by systems they do not control, this created recurring work and a common source of misconfiguration, where a protection was enabled in AWS WAF but the client-side integration was missing. Enabling automatic SDK integration on the web ACL protecting your CloudFront distribution removes that per-application work.

Automatic SDK integration is available for web ACLs that are used with Amazon CloudFront and contain at least one of those managed rule groups. You can configure it using the AWS Management Console, CLI, SDK, CDK, or CloudFormation. In the AWS WAF console, the setting appears with the managed rule group settings and is on by default for new web ACLs that you create with one of those rule group. When you create a web ACL programmatically, the setting is off by default. Web ACLs created before this release are unchanged.

There is no additional charge for automatic SDK integration. For requirements, limitations, and Content Security Policy guidance, see Automatic SDK integration for CloudFront distributions in the AWS WAF Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows and flow modules, simplifying how you build, test, and deploy customer experience flows while minimizing impact to live end-customer traffic. With this launch, you can now create immutable versions of a flow and attach one or more friendly names (i.e., aliases) to a version, then point resources such as queues, quick connects, and phone numbers at an alias instead of a specific version.

Rolling out a new version takes a single update, with no need to republish or relink each resource. For example, you can publish an updated customer experience flow as a new version and validate it in a test environment while live traffic stays on the current version, then repoint the production alias to move every phone number to the new version in a single update.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see Flow versioning and aliasing in the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics
items.summary:
Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch. The integration collects Kafka exporter metrics and consumer-group lag metrics from your Amazon MSK clusters.

Managed Prometheus collectors discover and collect Prometheus metrics from your workloads, so you don't run and operate collection agents yourself. You ingest the collected metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace or into Amazon CloudWatch, where you query and analyze them. You monitor Kafka stream health and consumer performance with consumer-group metrics. This helps you detect processing bottlenecks in your streaming applications.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where managed Prometheus collectors are generally available. To learn more, see the documentation for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch.

items.title: Amazon Quick Introduces Quick Essentials
items.summary:
Amazon Quick introduces Quick Essentials for enterprises. The plan makes it easier for organizations to get started with all the features of Quick such as AI-powered chat, Research, Flows, and Apps, and lets users view and interact with Quick Sight dashboards and reports and then manage adoption at the desired pace.

In AWS Regions where Amazon Quick is available, Quick Sight Reader users are upgraded to Quick Essentials at no additional per-user cost. With Quick Essentials, Quick Sight Readers can ask their dashboards questions in plain language, like what drove a revenue dip in March, and dig into the details with follow-up questions. They can turn the answer into a document, presentation, or spreadsheet for their team. When they need more context, Research pulls from their data, files, and the web into a detailed report with citations. If they need the same update every week, Flows can build it and send it automatically. When they need a tool that doesn't exist yet, like a request tracker, they can describe it and Apps builds it, without writing code.

Existing dashboards, Favorites, and Recents stay in place. Row-level and column-level security apply to every answer, and data is not shared across customers or used to train shared models. Administrators continue to manage the capabilities with custom permission profiles that can be applied to any user or a role.

Quick Essentials is enabled in a phased rollout across AWS Regions where Quick AI features are available. To learn more, read the Amazon Quick Community blog post. For pricing details, visit the Amazon Quick pricing page.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning, enabling you to run several models on a single GPU instead of dedicating a whole accelerator to each one. Using NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, SageMaker AI divides a GPU into as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers serving small and mid-size models, such as fine-tuned variants, embedding models, rerankers, and classifiers, previously had to give every model an entire accelerator, so an instance hosted no more models than it had GPUs and paid for GPU capacity those models could never use.

With GPU partitioning, you choose how to divide the GPUs behind your endpoint and place each model on a partition sized to fit it. Several models then share one accelerator with hardware-enforced isolation, so a busy model cannot take memory or throughput from the models beside it. Right-sizing an accelerator to a workload also opens up newer instance generations that would otherwise be more capacity than a single model needs. You configure GPU partitioning when you create an endpoint that hosts inference components, and you continue to invoke each model by name, so your application code doesn't change.

GPU partitioning is available on P4d, P5, G7, and G7e instances in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (Ireland). To learn more, visit the Amazon SageMaker AI deployment page and see the Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide.

items.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg table optimization in the US West (N. California) Region
items.summary:
AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports automatic table optimization for Apache Iceberg tables in the US West (N. California) Region. Apache Iceberg is an open table format that delivers fast query performance over large tables in data lakes. With this launch, you can enable table optimization for individual tables or for all tables in your Data Catalog.

Apache Iceberg tables accumulate small files, snapshots, and unreferenced files with every write, which slows queries and increases storage costs over time. Table optimization continuously monitors your tables to compact small files in the background, remove snapshots that are past your retention settings, and delete unreferenced files that are no longer needed. You can monitor each run from the AWS Glue console, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and logs.

You can enable table optimization using the AWS Glue console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. For the full list of Regions where table optimization is available, see Supported Regions for table optimizers. To learn more, see Optimizing Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue Developer Guide. To get started, visit the AWS Glue product page.

items.title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers — eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account.

From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. Partners can revoke a subsidiary authorization or a subsidiary connection at any time, which immediately stops that subsidiary from creating new offers — agreements and offers already extended to buyers remain unchanged.

This capability is available today at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, see  Managing subsidiary account connections  and  Creating private offers as a subsidiary account .

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle and SQL Server now support storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes
items.summary:
Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Amazon RDS for Oracle now support RDS storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes. RDS storage autoscaling automatically scales storage capacity in response to growing database workloads, with zero downtime.

Additional storage volumes allow you to add up to three additional volumes to increase your storage capacity up to 256 TiB. Previously, you had to manually provision storage capacity on the additional storage volumes based on anticipated application capacity demands while autoscaling could be enabled on the primary storage volume. Under-provisioning could result in application downtime, and over-provisioning could result in under-utilized resources and higher costs. With RDS storage autoscaling, you simply set your desired maximum storage limit for each additional storage volume, and autoscaling takes care of the rest.

RDS storage autoscaling continuously monitors actual storage consumption, and scales capacity up automatically when actual utilization approaches provisioned storage capacity. Autoscaling works with new and existing database instances. Autoscaling has no additional charges and you only pay for the provisioned storage resources. You can enable it by using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or Amazon RDS API.

RDS storage autoscaling for additional storage volumes is available for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Amazon RDS for Oracle in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, please visit the Amazon RDS storage autoscaling documentation.

items.title: Amazon Aurora now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can select cryptographic groups from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards.

Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our getting started page.

items.title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports updating connector plugins and worker configurations
items.summary:
Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now lets you update the custom plugin and worker configuration of an existing connector. This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency.

Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, updating a connector's plugin or worker configuration meant deleting the connector and recreating it - a disruptive operation that added risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can update a connector's plugin and worker configuration in place. The connector keeps its committed offsets, so its tasks continue processing from where they left off once the update completes.

This capability is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is supported. To learn more, visit Amazon MSK Connect developer guide.

items.title: AWS Step Functions workflows now available as AI agent tools
items.summary:
You can now use your AWS Step Functions workflows as tools for AI agents through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. Your agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. Agents can use your existing Standard and Express workflows as tools.

AWS Step Functions is a visual workflow service capable of orchestrating over 220 AWS services to help customers build distributed applications at scale. AgentCore Gateway connects AI agents to tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). With this launch, your agents can run multi-step business processes in the same order every time. For example, a customer support agent can start your refund workflow, and Step Functions runs the eligibility check, manager approval, and credit steps, so every refund follows your policy. Agents can also look up workflow runs, so an operations agent can tell your on-call engineer which order runs failed overnight and where, letting them go straight to fixing the step that broke.

This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway is available. You pay standard rates for Step Functions and AgentCore Gateway.

To get started, follow the tutorial in the Step Functions Developer Guide. For all supported operations and setup options, see Step Functions connector targets in the AgentCore Gateway documentation. If you build with an AI coding assistant such as Kiro, the Agent Toolkit for AWS gives it skills and guidance for building on AWS.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
items.summary:
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in two additional AWS Regions: Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town). DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to ten times performance improvement, from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second.

With DAX, you can accelerate read-intensive and bursty workloads such as real-time bidding, gaming leaderboards, and retail product catalogs, while offloading read traffic from your DynamoDB tables. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so you can add microsecond-latency caching to your applications with minimal code changes. Customers can now keep cached data within the Region and meet low-latency requirements while benefiting from a fully managed service, including automated patching and failover.

To learn more, see the Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator page. For the full list of Regions where DAX is available, see the AWS Regional Services page.

items.title: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade to Grafana version 13.2
items.summary:
Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade from Grafana version 12.4 to 13.2. Upgrading to version 13.2 brings features launched as part of open-source Grafana versions 13.0 to 13.2. These include Git Sync for dashboards, dynamic dashboards, and PromQL query support in the Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin.

With Git Sync, you can treat dashboards as code by linking a workspace to a Git repository. Dashboard modifications can be tracked, reviewed, and reverted through version control. Dynamic dashboards bring a more adaptable approach to layout and paneling. You can construct responsive views driven by conditions that respond to the data and variables in scope. With Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin support for Prometheus Query Language, you can use PromQL to query metrics that CloudWatch takes in via its OpenTelemetry (OTLP) endpoint, in addition to the existing Metric Search and Metrics Insights query types.

In-place upgrade to Grafana 13.2 is supported in all AWS regions where Amazon Managed Grafana is generally available. You can upgrade with just a few clicks from the AWS Console, AWS SDK or AWS CLI. For a complete list of new features, refer to Differences between Grafana versions in the Amazon Managed Grafana User Guide. For upgrade instructions, see Update your workspace version. To learn more about Amazon Managed Grafana features and its pricing, visit the product page and pricing page.

items.title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
items.summary:
AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP as source or destination locations. You can now run Windows to Windows transfers, such as from an on-premises file server to FSx for Windows File Server. Additionally, Enhanced mode agents can now run on Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization version 4.20 or later.

With this launch, you can use the same location options in Enhanced mode as in Basic mode. Enhanced mode processes data in parallel for higher performance, removes file count limitations, and provides detailed data transfer metrics. OpenShift Virtualization expands your agent deployment options alongside VMware ESXi, KVM, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Amazon EC2.

You can get started by choosing Enhanced mode when you create a task in the AWS DataSync console. These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS DataSync documentation.

items.title: ACM now supports ACME for public certificates in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) ACME protocol support is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West), providing a fully managed ACME server endpoint that issues public TLS certificates from Amazon Trust Services using any ACMEv2-compatible client, including Certbot, cert-manager for Kubernetes, and acme.sh. With the CA/Browser Forum mandating 47-day certificate lifetimes by 2029, manual management of public certificates becomes untenable. ACME support in ACM gives developers a standards-based path to fully automate certificate issuance and renewal.

To learn more, visit the AWS News blog post, the ACM ACME documentation, the ACM pricing page, and the AWS Regional Services page.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports SOCI-indexed images to start training jobs in seconds
items.summary:
Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces support for Seekable OCI (SOCI)-indexed container images for training and processing jobs, so your jobs start running your code sooner. SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, cutting GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90%, with no impact on training performance. Before a training or processing job can run, SageMaker AI downloads its container image to the instance. For deep learning images, which routinely exceed 10 GB, that download adds minutes to the start of every job, and you pay for that time. Now, when your image includes a SOCI index, SageMaker AI lazy-loads the image, fetching only the files needed to start the container and streaming the rest in the background as your code runs.

To use this feature, reference a SOCI-indexed image from a private Amazon ECR repository in your training or processing job. You can use a pre-indexed AWS Deep Learning Container by changing the image tag to its -soci variant, or add a SOCI index to your own image in Amazon ECR with open-source tools, without rebuilding the image. No changes to your job definition, entry point, or data channels are needed. SageMaker AI checks for an index automatically and images without an index download as before. If an index can't be used, the job falls back to a standard download and continues running.

SOCI-indexed images for SageMaker AI training and processing jobs are available today in all AWS Regions where SageMaker AI is available, through the SageMaker AI APIs, CLIs, SDKs, and Console. To learn more, see the documentation for training jobs and processing jobs, or read the launch blog.

items.title: Amazon Redshift announces hands-off automated cross-region backups
items.summary:
Amazon Redshift announces automated cross-region snapshot copy for Amazon Redshift. You can now have your Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup automatically backed up to the target AWS region(s) you choose. The automated cross-region snapshot copy feature will automatically, always copy the most recent snapshot with no manual intervention, continuously and incrementally and ensure your cluster is backed-up to the destination region(s), giving you additional options for business continuity.

The benefit to enabling the new automated cross-region snapshot copy feature is that you do not need to manually intervene to initiate a cross-region snapshot copy when an unplanned outage event occurs. Also, this feature takes the most recent snapshot available on your system to copy to the destination region, so you don't have to wait for the next snapshot to be taken, making it independent of your snapshot schedule on your local cluster. To configure cross-region snapshot copy, you need to enable the automated cross-region snapshot copy feature for each cluster and configure the destination region(s) to copy snapshots and how long to keep copied automated snapshots in the destination Region. You can choose the retention period for automated snapshots in the destination region. User snapshots are retained until you explicitly delete them. To restore the snapshot in the destination region, use the snapshot restore feature to a new provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup. Snapshots copied with the automated cross-region snapshot copy feature have names prefixed with `copy` in the destination region.

This feature is available in all regions AWS Commercial and GovCloud (US) regions.

For more details on configuration and usage see the Amazon Redshift documentation sections for cross-region snapshot copy: Amazon Redshift snapshots and backups. For details on restoring a cluster from a snapshot, see the documentation for Restoring a cluster from a snapshot. For pricing information, please review the 'Backup and storage' and 'Data transfer' sections of the Amazon Redshift pricing page.

items.title: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management and cross-account backup in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
items.summary:
AWS Backup now supports cross-account management, cross-account backup, and delegated administrators in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. These capabilities help you centrally manage, monitor, and copy backups across the accounts in your organization using AWS Organizations.

With cross-account management, you can deploy organization-wide backup policies from your AWS Organizations management account or a delegated administrator account. You can also monitor backup, copy, and restore jobs across all of your organization accounts from one place. With cross-account backup, you can copy recovery points to a backup vault in another account in your organization, which adds protection against accidental or malicious deletion in the source account. You can also register a member account as a delegated administrator, so your teams can manage backups across your organization without needing access to your management account.

There is no additional charge to use these capabilities; standard AWS Backup pricing applies. To learn more, see the AWS Backup documentation at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/. To get started, visit the AWS Backup console at https://console.aws.amazon.com/backup.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations, named permission sets that control what actions individual project members can perform. Previously, project members could only be assigned Owner or Contributor designations, which provided nearly identical permissions. With custom designations, administrators define permission sets that align with their organization's personas and assign them to project members. Designations govern all actions within a project, providing administrators with a single permission model for separation of duties.

Administrators create designations in the SageMaker Unified Studio administration portal by selecting permissions grouped into categories such as Catalog, Subscriptions, Connections, Notebooks, and Data Agent. For example, a "Data Steward" designation might include permissions to approve subscription requests and publish assets, while an "Analyst" designation is limited to querying data and running notebooks. Each designation is defined at the domain level and assigned across any project in that domain. When a member performs an action, SageMaker Unified Studio evaluates their assigned designation and permits or denies the request. Data engineers, stewards, analysts, and automated pipelines can now work within the same project with differentiated access, removing the need to create separate projects to isolate permissions. Every domain includes two managed designations, Owner and Contributor, and administrators can create up to 10 additional designations.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, visit the Designations documentation.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports the September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch (MRP) for Oracle Database version 19c and 26ai. An MRP is a minor engine version that builds on a quarterly Release Update (RU), bundling Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update (CSPU) with additional Oracle-recommended fixes. The September 2026 MRP is applied on top of the July 2026 RU and includes the Oracle September CSPU. We recommend upgrading to the September 2026 MRP as it includes the latest security updates for Oracle Database.

This release also includes the updated Oracle time zone file (DST version 46), which reflects the latest daylight saving time rule changes in several regions, including British Columbia and Alberta in Canada (effective November 1, 2026) and Morocco and Western Sahara (effective September 20, 2026), which are moving to permanent UTC offsets. If you store timestamps that include time zone information for these areas, the updated time zone file keeps that data aligned with the new rules.

You can apply the September 2026 MRP for new database instances, or upgrade existing instances to engine version 19.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-09.r2 or 26.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-09.r2 from the Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. To learn more about Oracle MRPs supported on Amazon RDS for each engine version, see the Amazon RDS for Oracle Release notes.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 is now available
items.summary:
AWS announces the general availability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 (@aws/agentcore 1.0.0), rebuilt with faster startup, a consistent command structure, and support for more AgentCore resources. The CLI helps developers create, develop, deploy, and operate AI agents and supporting resources from the terminal.

With version 1.0, developers can use the project workflow or work directly with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments without first adding them to a project. Developers can invoke existing resources by ID or ARN, open an interactive shell, export a harness, and use searchable menus, resource pickers, and guided workflows. Consistent global flags provide region selection, JSON output, debugging, and version information across commands.

Existing projects can be migrated to AgentCore version 1 using the agentcore migrate command.

Install AgentCore CLI version 1.0 from npm or explore the source on GitHub. To learn more, visit the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page, AgentCore CLI reference, and Get started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

items.title: Public endpoints for Amazon ElastiCache Serverless now in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports public endpoints in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. A public endpoint lets you connect to your cache from a serverless function or any application running outside a VPC, without setting up a VPN, a bastion host, or an SSH tunnel.

With a public endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless gives you a fully managed cache with no VPC to configure and no infrastructure to provision, and you can create one in under a minute. Every connection uses IAM authentication over TLS 1.3, so there's no password to store or rotate. Connect using Valkey GLIDE 2.2 or later, which has built-in IAM support, or another Valkey client paired with the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache, an open-source library that generates and refreshes IAM authentication tokens for you.

With this expansion, public endpoints for ElastiCache Serverless are now available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for using public endpoints beyond standard ElastiCache Serverless pricing.

To get started, create a Valkey 9.0 or later serverless cache with a public endpoint using the AWS Management Console, AWS SDK, or AWS CLI. To learn more about public endpoints, see Create a Valkey serverless cache with a public endpoint.

items.title: AWS Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading for Lambda Managed Instances
items.summary:
AWS Lambda now supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) for lazy loading Event Functions packaged as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images running on Lambda Managed Instances. With SOCI support, Lambda fetches only the files needed at each stage of the execution environment startup rather than downloading the entire image upfront, reducing container startup times by up to 70%.

Customers building compute-intensive applications such as data processing pipelines, high-throughput API backends, and batch computation workloads require substantial memory and CPU resources to process large datasets, serve low-latency responses at scale, and run complex computations efficiently. Container images for these workloads can reach several gigabytes, and downloading and preparing the full image can take several minutes when provisioning new execution environments. SOCI support on Lambda Managed Instances eliminates this bottleneck by streaming only the required files at each stage of the execution environment startup, so your functions start faster as you scale.

To get started, create a SOCI index (a table of contents for the files in your image layers) for your container image and push it to Amazon ECR. When creating or updating your function, set the image URI to the SOCI-indexed tag in Amazon ECR (for example, my-function:v1-soci) and publish a function version. Lambda automatically detects the SOCI index and enables lazy loading with no additional configuration. If you use a coding assistant such as Kiro, Claude Code, or Codex, install the Lambda Managed Instances skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS to configure and deploy functions through your agent.

The feature is available in all AWS commercial Regions where Lambda Managed Instances is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda Managed Instances developer guide.

items.title: Introducing time series collections for the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
items.summary:
Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection.

Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage.  With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. Alerting and anomaly detection are also now available, so customers can get notified about issues and spot unusual patterns in their log and event data without separate tooling.

Time series collections are available today in all AWS Regions where OpenSearch Serverless is available. To learn more about the pricing for the new warm storage,  see OpenSearch Serverless pricing. To learn more about time series collections on Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, see the OpenSearch Serverless feature page, the launch blog, and the AWS documentation.

items.title: Quick now supports smart approvals for agentic actions
items.summary:
Amazon Quick now supports smart approvals, a review layer that reduces unnecessary approval prompts while preserving human oversight of the actions that matter most. As agents take more actions on a user's behalf, such as sending email, updating records, and creating tickets, asking a person to approve every step leads to approval fatigue and weaker oversight over time. With smart approvals, a separate review model called the classifier evaluates each eligible action against the user's request. It approves routine actions automatically and refers consequential actions to the user for review.

Your existing policies always come first. Smart approvals only reviews actions where the user's setting is "ask" each time. Denied actions stay denied, and smart approvals never grants new access. The classifier sends higher-impact actions to the user for review. These include sending content outside the organization, changing permissions, deleting content, making payments, and actions that go beyond what the user asked for. Each automatic approval covers only the exact action that was reviewed. If a review fails or times out, the action goes to the user.

Smart approvals is on for all users by default. Administrators control who can use it with custom permissions, and users can turn it off for their conversations and scheduled runs in chat options. AWS CloudTrail records each action review made through smart approvals and each change to a user's smart approvals setting.

Smart approvals is available in Amazon Quick in all AWS Regions where Amazon Quick agentic capabilities are supported. For more information, see the AWS Region table.

To learn more about smart approvals, see smart approvals in the Amazon Quick User Guide. For more information about Amazon Quick, see the Amazon Quick product page.

items.title: Amazon EKS Dashboard now provides fleet-wide visibility into certificate authority (CA) rotation
items.summary:
Today, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) announces certificate authority (CA) rotation visibility in the Amazon EKS Dashboard, giving you a consolidated view of CA rotation across your clusters. The Amazon EKS Dashboard already provides centralized visibility into your clusters across AWS Regions and accounts, and it now includes CA rotation, so you can see where action is needed without checking each cluster individually.

Each Amazon EKS cluster has its own CA, and clusters created since 2018 have CAs with a 10-year validity period that are now approaching the point where rotation activities should begin. In the EKS Dashboard, you can now see your clusters and their CA rotation status, which clusters have CAs approaching expiration, and upcoming automated rotation events, so platform teams who operate many clusters can prioritize action across their fleet from one place.

The Amazon EKS Dashboard aggregates data across your accounts and Regions through AWS Organizations, so you enable trusted access for the dashboard in your organization’s management account to use this capability. You view the dashboard from the US East region (us-east-1), and it is available at no additional cost. CA rotation support extends to all commercial AWS Regions, and the dashboard brings that rotation status together in one fleet-wide view. To learn more, see the Amazon EKS documentation.

items.title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances adds cross-instance and Spot consolidation
items.summary:
Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available.

Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. Until now, optimization evaluated each instance in isolation for replacement, which worked well when a capacity provider was configured with diverse instance types. However, when a capacity provider was configured with a narrow range of instance types, there were fewer opportunities to consolidate multiple underutilized instances, because no single replacement could yield savings. With cross-instance consolidation, ECS now evaluates and repacks tasks across multiple instances simultaneously. For example, in our testing with a capacity provider configured for c9g instances with a minimum size of 4xlarge, running 261 tasks (each 1 vCPU, 1.94 GiB), cross-instance consolidation reduced the fleet from 19 instances (seven 4xlarge, seven 8xlarge, four 12xlarge, and one 24xlarge) to 13 instances (eight 4xlarge and five 8xlarge), while raising CPU utilization from 42% to 91% and memory utilization from 41% to 88%. Spot consolidation applies the same approach to Spot capacity, first verifying replacement capacity is available. With these enhancements, ECS Managed Instances delivers deeper cost optimization for both your On-Demand and Spot workloads.

Cross-instance and Spot consolidation are now available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions, and apply automatically to all existing and new ECS Managed Instances capacity providers. To learn more, see our documentation.

items.title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
items.summary:
AWS Lambda announces the Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter plugin for Lambda durable functions. This new observability plugin captures the step-by-step history of your durable executions and sends them to one or more destinations of your choice. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language.

Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. Destinations include Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 for Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon OpenSearch Service. You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a sampling rate to control data volume. With the MCP server, an on-call engineer can ask an AI agent to list recent failed executions and find the cause of a failure, and a business analyst can find all transactions for a specific customer.

The exporter is available for TypeScript, Python, Java, and Go. To get started, install the exporter, register the plugin in your function handler, then add the MCP server to your agent.

The Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter is available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions that support Lambda durable functions. To learn more, see the Durable Execution SDK documentation and the blog post.

items.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports Kubernetes Gateway API
items.summary:
Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API, giving customers a standard, portable way to define how traffic reaches their applications. Customers can configure application load balancing using Gateway and HTTPRoute resources, and EKS Auto Mode provisions and manages the underlying AWS infrastructure automatically.

With this launch, EKS Auto Mode customers can adopt the next-generation Kubernetes traffic management standard without installing or configuring a separate controller. Capabilities include HTTP and gRPC routing, cross-namespace traffic routing for multi-team environments, weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, and automatic TLS certificate discovery through AWS Certificate Manager. Existing workloads using Ingress resources continue to work alongside Gateway API resources.

To get started, see the Amazon EKS documentation. Gateway API support is included as part of EKS Auto Mode and is available in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is supported. Standard charges apply for the AWS load balancing resources provisioned.

items.title: AWS Backup adds restore testing support for Amazon Redshift
items.summary:
AWS Backup restore testing now supports Amazon Redshift. Restore testing helps you automate and periodically run restore tests of your backups, so you can confirm that your Amazon Redshift backups restore successfully and measure how long the restores take.

You can now include Amazon Redshift in your restore testing plans alongside other supported AWS resources across storage, compute, and database services. Restore testing plans automatically select recovery points, run restores on a schedule, and measure restore job completion time against your recovery time objectives (RTO). This helps you evaluate recovery readiness and meet regulatory and compliance requirements for disaster recovery and business continuity.

To get started, create a restore testing plan and assign your Amazon Redshift resources by Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or tag. Choose whether each test restores the latest or a random eligible recovery point. Optionally, use restore testing validation to confirm the restored resource before AWS Backup deletes the test resources.

This support is available in all AWS Regions where both restore testing and Amazon Redshift are supported by AWS Backup. You can use the AWS Backup console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs. For a complete list of supported Regions and features, visit the AWS Backup documentation. To learn more about restore testing, visit the product page and pricing page.

items.title: Kiro が自身のハーネスの性質を Lean で証明する
items.summary: Kiro が自身のコードの一部を Lean でモデル化し、そのモデルについての定理を証明し、各モデルを TypeScript、Rust、Python のコードと照らし合わせる作業を、自動で進める仕組みを作りました。最初に適用した対象は Kiro 自身です。

items.title: Amazon EVS と FSx for ONTAP 上で高可用性の Oracle Database を設計する
items.summary: VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) への既存投資がある企業は、アプリケーションの再設計や運用チームの再教育を行うことなく、Oracle データベースを AWS に移行したいと考えています。Amazon Elastic VMware Service (Amazon EVS) 上の Oracle は、既存の VMware 運用ワークフローを維持しながら、サブミリ秒のストレージレイテンシー、スナップショットベースのバックアップ、クロスリージョンディザスタリカバリ (DR)、および独立したストレージスケーリングを活用できます。 この記事では、Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP を使用して Amazon EVS 上に完全な Oracle Database 環境を設計する方法を紹介します。使い慣れた VMware 運用ツールを維持しながら、ストレージ、コンピューティング、ネットワーキング、ディザスタリカバリの各レイヤーがどのように連携して高可用性、クロスリージョン DR、サブミリ秒のストレージレイテンシーを実現するかを学びます。

items.title: Amazon EVS と FSx for ONTAP における Oracle Database のデプロイステップ
items.summary: この記事では、NFS データストアストレージとして Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP を使用して、Amazon Elastic VMware Service (Amazon EVS) 上に Oracle Database をデプロイするためのステップバイステップの手順を紹介します。ストレージボリュームのプロビジョニング、NFS データストアのマウント、Oracle のインストール、そしてクロスリージョンディザスタリカバリのための SnapMirror レプリケーションの設定を行います。 VMware 上で Oracle データベースを稼働させている企業は、再設計や再教育を行うことなく既存の運用ワークフローを維持できる AWS への移行パスを求めています。関連記事「Amazon EVS と FSx for ONTAP 上で高可用性の Oracle Database を設計する」では、Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) ベアメタルインスタンスの選択、VM のサイジング、vSAN と FSx for ONTAP 間でのストレージの分割、クロスリージョン DR のための SnapMirror レプリケーションの計画など、環境を設計する方法を説明しました。 この記事は、アーキテクチャ編の続きです。Oracle VM のプロビジョニングと FSx for ONTAP ボリュームの作成から、NFS データストアのマウント、Oracle 19c のインストール、SnapMirror と SnapCenter の設定まで、スタック全体をデプロイするためのステップバイステップの手順を紹介します。また、既存のオンプレミス Oracle ワークロードを Amazon EVS に移行するための 4 つの移行パスと、スナップショットバックアップ、ポイントインタイムリカバリ、データベースクローニングを含む Day 2 運用についても説明します。

items.title: 【開催報告】フロンティア AI 時代のサイバー攻撃に備える ― 臨時開催 AWS セキュリティセミナー
items.summary: 2026年10月23日と30日に、臨時のAWSセキュリティセミナー「フロンティアAI時代のサイバー攻撃に備える」をオンラインで開催しました。AWSが基盤側で行っている対策と、AWS WAF、Amazon Inspector、AWS Security Agentなどお客様の側で取り組める対策を、2回分まとめてご報告します。11月からは週次のオンラインハンズオンも開催しています。

items.title: 週刊生成AI with AWS – 2026/10/26 週
items.summary: 今週の「週刊生成 AI with AWS」は、ドコモSMTBネット銀行が Amazon Connect Customer AI agents で電話とチャットの自動応対を始めた国内事例や、AMOREPACIFIC が Kiro でレガシー SAP ECC に AI 駆動開発を導入した事例を紹介しています。 サービスアップデートでは、Amazon Bedrock での OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra の一般提供、Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI 1.0 の公開、AWS Step Functions のワークフローを AI エージェントのツールとして使える機能などを取り上げています。 Kiro では、ハロウィンハッカソン Kiroween 2026 の開始、11 月 1 日からの新しい無料トライアル、週 1,000 件の PR を支える Kiro Crew チームの品質管理の記事をまとめています。
categories: AWSサービスアップデートまとめ

items.title: AI ガードレールによるコンタクトセンターでの責任ある AI の実装
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer のネイティブ機能 AI ガードレールは、コンタクトセンターにおける AI の安全で倫理的な導入を実現します。本記事では、プロンプト攻撃検出、コンテンツフィルタリング、PII 保護、コンテキストグラウンディングなど 7 つの保護コンポーネントの詳細と、AWS の責任ある AI フレームワークの 8 つの側面に沿った実装ガイダンスを解説します。

items.title: Kiro のハロウィンハッカソン Kiroween 2026 が始まりました
items.summary: Kiro が毎年ハロウィンの時期に開いているハッカソン Kiroween が、今年も始まりました。提出の締め切りは日本時間 2026 年 12 月 5 日（土）午前 7 時で、賞金の総額は 10 万ドルです。

items.title: Spec it safe：セキュリティ要件で仕様をハードニングし、シフトレフトを実現する
items.summary: spec 駆動開発 (SDD) は、大規模なチームのソフトウェア開発のやり方を変えつつあります。プロンプトだけに頼るのではなく spec を書き、それに沿って AI コーディングエージェントに設計、タスク、実装を進めさせます。

items.title: エージェント時代の運用：re:Invent 2026 の AIOps セッション
items.summary: re:Invent 2026 のクラウド運用トラックから、AI エージェントによるインシデント調査、修復、リリース検証、監査、モダナイゼーションを扱う AIOps セッションをテーマ別に紹介します。AWS DevOps Agent の事例やハンズオンを含め、目的に応じた推奨ルートもまとめます。
